items.0: I understand trading is risky and I can lose some or all of my funds.
items.1: I’m responsible for complying with the laws of my country of residence and/or citizenship.
items.2: My activity may have tax implications, and reporting them is my responsibility.
items.3: Pairlens includes advanced tools — not all of them are suitable for beginners.
items.4: Crypto and equities are real assets; their value can be volatile and change frequently.
items.5: When I connect an exchange or broker I use my own account and accept their terms of service, including any fees they charge on my trades or holdings.
items.6: Pairlens does not back up my API keys or wallets by design. I alone keep backups, and Pairlens cannot recover lost funds — especially crypto wallets.
items.7: Pairlens is an early preview (Beta), may contain bugs, and is provided “as is” with no warranty or liability. I’ll report issues I find.

intro.title: Every market, one list
intro.description: Live prices for CEX, DEX and equities stream side by side. Search anything, sort by what's moving, and click a row to open its chart.

watchlist.description: Star a pair to pin it to your watchlists, and let the movers rail surface the biggest gainers and losers of the session.

overview.title: Candles straight from the venue
overview.description: Real-time candles stream directly from the exchange — no middleman. Switch timeframes, hover for exact values, and dig into price action.

signals.title: Signals on every close
signals.description: Deterministic strategies read each candle as it closes and mark APPROVE, BLOCK and WATCH setups right on the chart.

plugins.publisherKeysDescription: Plugins only install when their signature matches a trusted publisher key. Add a key here to trust plugins from a self-hosted or company registry. Only add keys you received from a source you trust — anyone holding the matching private key can publish plugins that may request full access to your terminal.
plugins.publisherKeysEmpty: No custom keys. Official Pairlens publishers are always trusted.
plugins.publisherKeyIdInvalid: Key IDs are lowercase letters, digits and dashes (2–64 chars).
plugins.publisherKeyIdReserved: This ID is reserved for a built-in Pairlens key.
plugins.publisherKeyIdDuplicate: A key with this ID is already trusted.
plugins.publisherKeyValueInvalid: Not a valid Ed25519 public key (expected 32 bytes, base64-encoded).
plugins.publisherKeyConsentBody: Plugins signed with this key will be installable on this device. A malicious publisher can ship plugins that request full trust — with access to your other plugins' data, stored exchange credentials, and trading. Compare the fingerprint with the publisher through a channel you trust before continuing.

security.lockDescription: Ask for a password before this terminal can be used on this device.
security.turnOffDescription: Enter your current password to remove the lock from this device.
security.noRecoveryWarning: There is no password recovery. If you forget it, the only way back in erases this device's data. Save it in your password manager now.
security.triggersDescription: Choose the moments the password prompt should appear.
security.triggerStartupHint: Ask for the password on a cold start.
security.triggerIdleHint: Lock after {{minutes}} minutes with no mouse or keyboard.
security.triggerPeriodicHint: Lock again after a fixed time, however busy the session is.
security.triggerWakeHint: Lock when the machine comes back from sleep.
security.triggerTradeHint: Confirm an order you place by hand or through the copilot, including auto-approved proposals. Bots are never asked.
security.protectsBody: It puts a full-screen password prompt in front of the terminal, so someone at your desk cannot click around your positions, read your balances, or place an order. It encrypts nothing: your exchange API keys and wallet keys stay exactly where they were, and anyone with your unlocked computer and some technical skill can read this app’s local data without ever seeing the prompt.
security.protectsBots: Armed bots keep trading while the terminal is locked. Locking the screen is not pausing your strategies.
security.protectsDesktop: Your password check is stored in the system keychain and never leaves this computer.
security.protectsBrowser: This build stores the password check in browser storage. Clearing site data removes the lock. The desktop app is the supported home for this.
security.lockNowDescription: Close settings and lock the terminal immediately.
security.resetConfirmBody: This erases every exchange API key, wallet key, workspace, chart layout and chat on this computer. There is no undo and no password recovery. If you are signed in, settings that sync to the cloud come back when you sign in again — API keys and wallet keys never do, because they are only ever stored here.
security.vaultDescription: Encrypt your exchange API keys and wallet keys with a password or a passkey.
security.vaultAlsoUnlocks: Any of these also unlocks the terminal lock screen — one password serves both.
security.biometricNeedsVault: Set up the vault with a password first — Touch ID is then added on top.
security.vaultRemoveLastBlocked: This is the only way into your vault. Add another before removing it.
security.vaultRemoveBiometricOnlyBlocked: Touch ID cannot be the only way in — the fingerprints on this Mac can change. Keep a password or a passkey.
security.vaultProtectsBody: With a vault, your API keys and wallet keys are stored encrypted. Someone who copies this browser profile — or this computer's disk — gets ciphertext they cannot open without your password or your passkey.
security.vaultCeiling: It does not protect keys while you are using them. Anything running inside this page can ask the unlocked vault for a key, the same way the app does. The desktop app remains the recommendation for your most valuable keys.
security.vaultNoRecovery: There is no recovery. Lose every way in and the encrypted keys are gone — the only way back into the app erases this device's data.
security.vaultDesktopToggleHint: Your keys are already in the system keychain. Turn this on to add a password or a passkey on top.
security.vaultDesktopOptOutBody: Your keys go back to being protected by the system keychain alone. Nothing is deleted, and you can turn the vault back on later.
security.vaultMigrated_one: Moved 1 key you already had into the vault.
security.vaultMigrated_other: Moved {{count}} keys you already had into the vault.
security.vaultMigrationFailed: Vault setup did not finish. Your keys are still readable — open the vault to complete it.
security.vaultSharedBackoff: The vault and the lock screen share one attempt limit, so too many wrong passwords delays both.
security.vaultCliNote: The command-line tool takes API keys as arguments and never reads the vault.
security.hardLockDescription: Lock the vault, not just the screen.
security.hardLockWarning: Locks the vault, not just the screen. Live bots and automations stop trading until you unlock. Paper bots keep running.
security.hardLockConfirmBody: Live bots and automations stop trading until you unlock again. Paper bots keep running.

botsPage.localBody: Your strategies execute here, in Pairlens — not on a server we operate. That is what keeps your keys and your logic yours. The tradeoff is real: quit Pairlens or let this computer sleep and your bots stop with it, and an open position is left unwatched until you come back.
botsPage.emptyDescription: A bot is one of your strategy scripts deployed to a market. Pick a script, a pair and a size, and it starts trading on paper.
botsPage.emptyHeadline: Let a strategy watch the chart for you
botsPage.templateEmaCross: Follows the trend both ways: long above the cross, short below it.
botsPage.templateRsiReversion: Buys oversold dips, but only while price holds above its long trend.
botsPage.templateBreakout: Enters on a channel break confirmed by volume, and trails the move.
botsPage.pickBot: Pick a bot on the left to open it.
botsPage.chartPnlEmpty: Nothing realized yet. This traces the running total as each round trip closes.
botsPage.chartVolumeEmpty: No fills yet. This tracks the quote value the bot has moved, entries and exits both.
botsPage.chartTradesEmpty: No closed trades yet. Each bar counts the round trips that closed that day.
botsPage.tradesEmpty: No trades yet. The ledger fills in as the bot enters and exits.
botsPage.eventsEmpty: No events yet. Signals, orders and guard blocks are logged here.
botsPage.liveTradingHint: Route real orders to the venue instead of simulating fills. Turning this off stops the bot.

botsPage.createDescription: Deploy one of your strategy scripts to a market.
botsPage.noStrategiesDescription: A bot trades what a script declares: when to enter, when to exit, and how much to commit. Only meta = strategy(...) declares those. A script built with indicator(...) draws on the chart and nothing more, so there is nothing for a bot to execute.

botsPage.reasonIndicator: Indicator — needs a strategy(...) meta to run as a bot

botsPage.marketHint: The bot evaluates on this pair's closed candles at this timeframe.
botsPage.sizingHint: How much the bot commits when the strategy signals an entry.
botsPage.guardsDescription: Limits enforced outside the strategy. Leave a field blank for no limit.
botsPage.guardDailyLossHint: Stop the bot once today's realized losses reach this share of equity.
botsPage.guardTradeCapHint: Stop the bot after this many entries in a rolling 24 hours.
botsPage.guardPositionCapHint: Never hold more than this notional.

pluginStore.buildOwnDescription: Pairlens is an open platform. Scaffold a plugin, build it, and load it locally — no registry required.
pluginStore.buildStepScaffoldNote: Inside this monorepo, use: bun run create:plugin my-plugin
pluginStore.buildStepBuildNote: Produces a single .zip (manifest.json + module.js + optional styles.css).
pluginStore.buildStepInstallNote: Go to the Installed tab and use
pluginStore.buildStepInstallNote2: — or, on desktop, drop the folder into the plugins directory.
pluginStore.buildRuntimeNote: The host provides React, @pairlens/plugin-sdk (hooks), the @pairlens/ui design system (import from the package root), and @pairlens/fast-financial-charts at runtime — mark them external in your build. Design-system components are styled by the host; for custom CSS, ship a styles.css with your plugin.
pluginStore.buildExamplesNote: See the dev-starter and dev-sync examples in the repo for working references.

accounts.storedSecurelyDetail: All credentials are stored securely on your computer using the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or Linux Secret Service), which encrypts them at rest. They are never sent to or stored on Pairlens servers. Make sure to always keep a backup of your API keys in a safe place.

localOnly.badgeAria: Learn how your keys are kept private
localOnly.title: Your keys never leave this device
localOnly.subtitle: Here is exactly what happens to the API keys and wallet keys you add.
localOnly.deviceBody: Your exchange API keys and wallet keys are saved on this computer and nowhere else — never uploaded to Pairlens or anyone.
localOnly.osBodyDesktop: They are kept in {{vault}} — the same protected vault your device uses for its own passwords, encrypted on disk.
localOnly.osBodyBrowser: They are encrypted on this device before being saved. The Pairlens desktop app keeps them in {{vault}}, your system's protected vault.
localOnly.openSourceTitle: Public source code — verify it yourself
localOnly.openSourceBody: Pairlens's code is public. You, a developer friend, or even an AI can read it and confirm your keys really do stay put.
localOnly.reassurance: Pairlens servers never receive your keys — not even when you are signed in.
